comparison: Perfect agreement on intravital imaging findings (C3, C48-C53). Both evaluations support the motility and clustering observations of LLPCs. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative analysis and temporal progression, while peer reviewers highlight this as enabling 'higher resolution analysis' than previously possible.

Strong agreement on CXCR4 findings (C7-C9, C61-C70, C93-C94). Both evaluations support the retention and survival role of CXCR4. Peer reviewers explicitly praised this as a major contribution with 'new aspects,' while OpenEval notes the incomplete deletion (C94) may underestimate effects.

Complete agreement on BEC-YFP model validation (C88-C92). Both evaluations strongly support the genetic timestamping system. Peer reviewers described it as 'clever and functional,' while OpenEval emphasizes the critical importance of specificity and efficient labeling for interpreting subsequent experiments.

Partial disagreement on RNA-seq and marker findings (C5-C6, C54-C55, C71-C79, C95-C100). OpenEval finds claims supported by deep sequencing and flow cytometry validation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting limited novelty ('already made by other groups') and unknown functional importance of transcriptome differences, suggesting need for human validation.

Disagreement on BCR repertoire interpretation (C10-C14, C82-C87). OpenEval supports non-random specification inference based on convergent metrics. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, raising concerns that polyclonal (vs antigen-specific) labeling may confound interpretation of repertoire features independently of longevity.

Agreement on PC turnover data (C39-C47). Both evaluations support the flow cytometry findings and age-dependent differences. Peer result also includes C15 and C59 (quasi-LLPC accumulation), which OpenEval addresses separately in R7. Peer reviewers note alignment with other groups' observations.

Agreement on LLPC clustering and APRIL dependence (C4, C35-C37). Both evaluations support these observations. OpenEval notes APRIL knockout data is from prior work rather than new experiments. Peer reviewers accepted clustering as a key strength without critique.

Strong disagreement on competitive niche model (C16). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes claim is speculative without direct competition evidence. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, explicitly stating 'no evidence presented here that these niches are limiting' and citing contradictory evidence from Robinson et al. (2023).

Overlap on surface marker findings (C54-C58). OpenEval supports flow cytometry validation of markers including CD93 bimodality and 6-marker enrichment. These claims are embedded in peer R4's broader UNCERTAIN evaluation of transcriptome/marker findings, where reviewers question novelty and functional importance.

Overlap on IgM enrichment in young splenic LLPCs (C80-C81). OpenEval supports this as a striking finding suggesting early specification. Peer R6 includes these claims in broader UNCERTAIN evaluation of repertoire analysis, with concerns about polyclonal vs antigen-specific confounding.

Overlap on quasi-LLPC accumulation with age (C15, C59). OpenEval supports the flow cytometry data but notes C16 (competition claim) is speculative. Peer R1 supports the accumulation findings as part of broader acceptance of the timestamping approach and age-related observations.

OpenEval evaluated background/introduction claims (C1-C2, C17-C34) as appropriately referenced established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically focus on novel findings rather than cited background.
